Today DaemonOptions.ResolveModel (src/Hall9k.Daemon/DaemonOptions.cs near line 799) calls AgentModel.Resolve(taskModel, ModelByRole.For(role), projectModel, DefaultModel), so the node\\u0027s per-role value beats the project\\u0027s single value (Decisions Log #33). This task flips the middle two so the project\\u0027s value beats the node\\u0027s role value; the verify and final-pass chains (ResolveVerifyReviewModel near line 821, ResolveFinalFullPassModel near line 848) and ResolveCourierModel near line 877 follow the same reorder. Update the doc comments, PLAN.md\\u0027s #33 projection if it states the order, docs/cli.md and docs/concepts.md where they describe the chain, and the existing resolution tests. No project on Brian\\u0027s fleet sets a project model today (verified with h9k project show on all four Mac projects, 2026-09-26), so nothing live changes behavior. Not stacked on 6fe2f5a2: the two touch different functions and can merge in either order; both should be released before effort is documented as mirroring the model chain. Dispatched sessions must not run install, update, join, or reconcile against the live install. Brian\\u0027s ruling on the pass knobs, 13:0x EDT: option (a), the project\\u0027s model beats the review-verify and final-pass knobs too, so a project model is a blanket statement with no hidden holes. Verified against main at a1237be0e (unchanged by v0.10.51 in these files). The order is coded once: AgentModel.Resolve (src/Hall9k.Domain/Shared/ValueObjects/AgentModel.cs near line 108), positional (task, role, project, platform) with role and project both AgentModel?, so a swap compiles silently; callers are DaemonOptions.ResolveModel near line 799 and ResolveCourierModel near line 877 (positional) and TaskStartCommand.ResolveBuildModelAsync near line 636 (named arguments, shared by TaskDelegateCommand near line 448). ResolveVerifyReviewModel near line 813 and ResolveFinalFullPassReviewModel near line 840 check the task, then their own node knob, then delegate to ResolveModel(Review); under (a) they check task, project, knob, then review\\u0027s chain. After the flip a project\\u0027s --model also beats --model-courier above the Sonnet floor; consequence for the context: a project model chosen for builds drags the deliberately cheap courier up over a node\\u0027s cheaper courier choice; no fleet project sets one today. Text pinned by tests: OperatingSettingsRendering.FallthroughDescription near lines 206 to 217 and OperatingSettingsRenderingTests near line 127. Docs stating the order: docs/getting-started.md near line 243, docs/operations.md near lines 1046 and 1084, docs/cli.md near lines 1059 and 1507; docs/concepts.md states no order. Help strings: TaskAddCommand.cs near line 249, ProjectSetCommand.cs near line 161. ProjectSettingsChanged (the only carrier of a project\\u0027s model) is node-scoped, so a project model never travels; only the node\\u0027s own operator sets it.
